reviewer: Claude Opus 5.5, curriculum and design work delegated by George
factChecks: Independently recomputed all 118 numeric keys from the problem statements in packages/curriculum/tests/astronomy-content.test.ts: 58 lesson and practice answers, 24 recall answers and 36 course-check answers. Every tolerance is checked to be no wider than the stated rounding (whole-number rounding or 2%).

Verified the OpenStax Astronomy 2e licence on the book's preface page on 6 October 2026: the current web edition is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, not CC BY 4.0, so all 22 cited sections are recorded as reference only. All prose, problems, drawings and the cover are original.

Checked formulas and values against the cited OpenStax sections: Kepler's laws (3.1), the 23.5° tilt, perihelion in January and the 3% distance variation (4.2), parallax d = 1/p and 1 pc = 3.26 ly (19.2), Wien's law and the Stefan-Boltzmann law (5.2), main-sequence lifetimes such as 500 million years at 3.3 solar masses (22.1), end states by initial mass from Table 23.1 (23.2), and the 2.73 K background released about 380,000 years after the Big Bang at about 3,000 K (29.4).

Checked physical constants against NASA NSSDCA fact sheets: Earth GM 3.986 × 10^14 m^3/s^2, radius 6,371 km, obliquity 23.44°, orbital speed 29.78 km/s, escape speed 11.186 km/s; Sun GM, luminosity 3.828 × 10^26 W and 5,772 K; Moon GM, radius, 384,400 km, 29.53-day synodic month and 5.145° inclination; Mars and Jupiter GM, radii and periods. The course uses a 23.4° tilt and states it in every problem.

Stated approximations explicitly: 15° per hour for the sky's turning, the power laws t ∝ M^-2.5 and L ∝ M^3.5, approximate eclipse limits of 1.0° and 1.5° of lunar latitude, a solar tide of 0.46 of today's lunar tide, H0 = 70 km/s/Mpc with the 67–73 range named, and 1/H0 as an estimate rather than the age.

Fifteen bounded model kinds have engine tests for physical invariants (zenith and pole altitude, equal areas swept in twelve equal-time sectors, vis-viva and escape speeds matching NASA values, inverse-square flux of 1,361 W/m^2 at 1 AU, Wien peaks, L = R^2 T^4, lifetimes) and component tests for keyboard case switching, scrubbing, finite playback, reduced motion and concealed results.
Checked that no beat diagram or course-check visual states the answer to its own question before grading; eleven check items were rewritten after this review found their givens exposed the answer.
Editorial review is by the authoring agent under delegated authority. There has been no independent human subject review or documented learner trial.
changes: Added a twelve-lesson introductory astronomy course in four modules with 72 questions (7 multiple choice, 7 single-term answers, 58 calculations), 24 recall cards and 48 answered visual beats with 108 authored cases.
Added twelve-item placement, mixed checkpoint and seven-day delayed application sets.
Added the astronomy explorer: fifteen deterministic model kinds drawn as layered SVG with finite playback, keyboard controls and reduced-motion handling.
